344-2:
Existing measures of AI and work score *exposure* of occupations to generative AI (Felten et al. 2021; Eloundou et al. 2024; Gmyrek et al. 2025). They do not measure *delegability*: whether an AI agent with tool use and computer use can carry out a task end to end. They are also mostly built on the U.S. O*NET classification, which most countries do not use. We build the Agent Delegability Index (ADI): every O*NET 30.2 task statement (18,796) is rated by several frontier language models with a fixed three-level rubric (augmentation, partial delegation, full delegation), validated against three independent human raters on a stratified sample of 1,500 tasks, mapped to ISCO-08 unit groups, and aggregated to countries with ILOSTAT employment by occupation. We test whether delegable employment is distributed unequally across countries by income level.

H1 (delegation divide). The share of employment in tasks rated delegable (level 2 or 3) is LOWER in low- and lower-middle-income countries than in high-income countries. Operationally: in a country-level regression of ADI_c on log GDP per capita (PPP, constant 2021 USD), the slope is positive (one-sided test).
 H2 (adoption gap). Among countries with Anthropic Economic Index usage data, the standardized gap between technical delegability (ADI_c) and observed AI usage per working-age person is larger in middle-income countries than in high-income countries (one-sided).
 H3 (convergent validity). Occupation-level ADI correlates positively with Eloundou et al. (beta) and Felten et al. (AIOE), with Pearson r between 0.40 and 0.80 for each (r > 0.80 would indicate ADI adds little beyond exposure; r < 0.40 would question validity).
 H4 (task length). The probability that a task is rated fully delegable (level 3) follows an inverted U in log human task duration (minutes_human): positive linear and negative quadratic coefficient in a logistic regression.
 ---
344-14:
Registration prior to creation of the outcome data. The delegability ratings (the outcome) do not exist at registration. Inputs are existing public data that we have downloaded but not analysed against any delegability outcome: O*NET 30.2 task statements and ratings, ESCO v1 occupations and skills, ILOSTAT employment by ISCO-08, World Bank income classification and GDP per capita, Anthropic Economic Index, comparison indices (Felten AIOE, Eloundou et al., Webb, Eisfeldt et al., ILO 2025), and household survey microdata (Colombia GEIH, Brazil PNADC, Mexico ENOE, Peru ENAHO).

Before registration we inspected only coverage: number of tasks per ISCO-08 group after the crosswalk (433 of 436 unit groups covered; 403 distinct task sets), and the number of countries with ILOSTAT employment by occupation (1-digit ISCO-08: 173 countries, 151 with data from 2019 onward; 2-digit availability being assessed). One author (CEM) previously rated a subset of O*NET tasks for generative-AI augmentation (arXiv 2604.01066); that construct and rubric differ from ADI and those ratings are not used.

Pilot ratings (300 tasks with each model, plus the format tests described under Study design) were generated before registration and are discarded. From them we inspected only JSON validity, run time, cost and agreement between formats and between models; we did not tabulate pilot ratings by occupation, income group or country.
344-38: Human raters are blind to all model ratings and to each other's ratings; each receives the same 1,500 tasks in an independent random order (seeds 20261021–20261023). Models are queried one task per call, with no other tasks, ratings or conversation history in context.
344-40:
Unit of rating: O*NET 30.2 task statement with its O*NET occupation title. Rubric (attached, frozen): reference technology = publicly available AI agents as of October 2026 (tool use, code execution, browsing, computer use; no robotics). Output per task: level (0 none, 1 augmentation, 2 partial delegation, 3 full delegation), share_delegable (0–100), minutes_human, four barrier flags (physical, accountability, trust, access) and confidence.

Raters: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (primary; model id claude-sonnet-5-5) and Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5), queried one task per call through the Claude Code command-line interface (claude -p, version 2.1.306) in a neutral configuration: no tools, no MCP servers, no session persistence, and a fixed one-line system prompt ("You are an expert rater of occupational tasks. Follow the user instructions exactly.") in place of the Claude Code system prompt. The interface does not expose temperature, so stability is measured directly: 100 randomly drawn tasks are rated twice by each model and test-retest agreement is reported. The model id returned by the interface and its version are logged for every call. The OpenAI, Google and open-weights raters named in earlier drafts are dropped before registration; no model is added or dropped after seeing main-run results.

Pilot (completed before registration, discarded): 300 tasks (seed 20261020). It checked JSON compliance (100%), cost and run time, and two format choices: (a) batches of 25 tasks per call, rejected by a rule fixed in advance (quadratic-weighted kappa against single calls 0.60 for Sonnet and 0.56 for Haiku, below the 0.80 threshold); (b) the interface wrapper: with the default Claude Code system prompt the mean level was higher than with the neutral configuration (quadratic kappa 0.70 between the two; Sonnet test-retest under the default wrapper 0.84). We register the neutral configuration as primary because it matches the single-call design and contains no self-description of the model as an agent; the default wrapper is a preregistered sensitivity analysis (see Other planned analyses).
344-44:
Pilot sample, human-validation sample and rater orderings are drawn with fixed seeds (20261020 and 20261021–20261023).

344-47:
Task–occupation bridge: O*NET-SOC 2019 → O*NET-SOC 2010 (O*NET Center crosswalk) → SOC 2010 → ISCO-08 (Hardy, Keister and Lewandowski, IBS). Task weights within O*NET occupation: importance × mean frequency, normalised. A SOC code mapping to k ISCO groups splits its weight 1/k. Military groups (0110, 0210, 0310) are excluded (no O*NET tasks). Seven residual ISCO groups without own O*NET tasks inherit the tasks of their 3-digit parent and are flagged as imputed. Code: datos/construir_crosswalk.py.
 Human validation: 1,500 tasks stratified by ISCO-08 major group, allocated in proportion to world employment (ILOSTAT) with a minimum of 60 per group (validacion/muestra.py). Three raters with at least a university degree in economics, engineering or social science, trained on the rubric with 20 practice tasks that are not in the sample.
344-51: All 18,796 O*NET 30.2 task statements; 433 ISCO-08 unit groups; all countries with ILOSTAT employment by occupation for a year ≥ 2019 (currently 151); 1,500 tasks × 3 human raters.
344-53: The task and occupation sets are the full population of the source classification. For human validation, 1,500 tasks give a 95% confidence-interval half-width below 0.03 for Krippendorff's alpha around 0.6 and at least 60 tasks per major group.
344-55:
Not applicable (full population). Model calls that fail validation are retried up to five times.

344-62: Per task and model: level (0–3), share_delegable (0–100), minutes_human, barrier_physical, barrier_accountability, barrier_trust, barrier_access, confidence. Per country: employment by ISCO-08 group (ILOSTAT), World Bank income group (FY2026), GDP per capita PPP, AI usage per working-age person (Anthropic Economic Index, latest release).
344-66:
Task consensus level: the modal level across models; with two models, the common level when they agree and the lower level when they disagree. Sonnet alone is reported as the primary-rater variant. Task share: median share_delegable across models. Occupation index (primary): ADI_o = Σ_t w_ot · 1[level_t ≥ 2]. Variants: ADI3_o with 1[level_t = 3]; ADIs_o = Σ_t w_ot · share_t/100. Country index: ADI_c = Σ_g e_cg · ADI_g / Σ_g e_cg, at the finest ISCO-08 level the country reports (2 digits if available for a year ≥ 2019, otherwise 1 digit). Within a reported group, unit-group ADIs are averaged with employment weights from countries in the same World Bank income group that report finer detail (pooled), and with equal weights as a sensitivity check. Headline: world ADI = employment-weighted mean of ADI_c over all included countries.
 ---
344-71: H1: OLS of ADI_c on log GDP per capita PPP; also with income-group dummies (reference: high income). One-sided test of the slope. H2: OLS of the standardized gap z(ADI_c) − z(usage_c) on income-group dummies; one-sided test that the middle-income coefficients are positive relative to high income. H3: Pearson and Spearman correlations of ADI_o with Eloundou beta and Felten AIOE after mapping both to ISCO-08 with the same bridge. H4: Logistic regression of 1[level = 3] on log(minutes_human) and its square, task level, standard errors clustered by occupation. Agreement: Krippendorff's alpha (ordinal) and quadratic-weighted kappa, human–human and human–model consensus.
344-75: Log of GDP per capita and of minutes_human (minutes winsorised at 1 and 4,800). Country indices standardized to mean 0, SD 1 for H2.
344-77: alpha = 0.05, one-sided for H1, H2 and the directional H4 terms. Confidence intervals by nonparametric bootstrap over tasks (1,000 draws; tasks resampled within occupation) propagated to occupation and country indices. Human–model alpha ≥ 0.60 is the acceptance threshold for the primary rater; results are reported whatever the value.
344-79: Military ISCO groups; countries whose latest ILOSTAT occupation data predate 2019; tasks whose ratings fail validation after five retries for a given model (excluded for that model only; counts reported).
344-81: Missing importance or frequency ratings in O*NET are imputed with the median; a country without GDP per capita is dropped from H1 but kept in the headline. No other imputation.
344-83:
Barrier decomposition (physical vs accountability vs trust vs access); gender, age and informality gradients using GEIH, PNADC, ENOE and ENAHO; robustness with ESCO essential skills instead of O*NET tasks; permutation placebo (tasks shuffled across occupations, 1,000 draws); comparison with the ILO 2025 index and the Agentic Adoption Index; model-by-model results. Wrapper sensitivity: the 1,500 human-validation tasks are re-rated by both models under the default Claude Code system prompt, and human-model agreement is compared between wrappers. Within-group weights: ILOSTAT publishes no 4-digit employment, so 4-digit groups are weighted within each reported 1- or 2-digit group by Colombian GEIH employment (2024–2026) for all countries, with equal weights as sensitivity. All are labelled exploratory in the paper.
